Wrap a custom function as a labeled estimator

Source: R/declare_estimator.R
label_estimator.Rd

label_estimator() returns a function suitable for use as .method in declare_estimator() or declare_test(): it fits the model, tidies the fit, tags the result with estimator and inquiry columns, and keeps the terms asked for. label_test() is the same function under a second name, kept so that 1.x scripts run; a test is an estimator whose tidied output carries a p-value, and nothing in the wrapper depends on which name was called. 1.x's fn = argument is .method = in both.

Usage

label_estimator(
  .method,
  label = NULL,
  inquiry = NULL,
  term = NULL,
  .summary = tidy_try
)

label_test(
  .method,
  label = NULL,
  inquiry = NULL,
  term = NULL,
  .summary = tidy_try
)

Arguments

.method

(required) A function that fits a model from data and ....

label

(optional) Estimator label, written to the estimator column. NULL (the default) adds no column.

inquiry

(optional) Inquiry label (or list of labels); the first is written to the inquiry column. NULL (the default) adds no column.

term

(optional) Character vector of terms to keep. NULL (the default) keeps every term.

.summary

(optional) Function for tidying the model fit. Defaults to tidy_try().

Value

A function of data and ... that calls .method(data = data, ...), tidies the fit with .summary, and returns the resulting tibble with the estimator and inquiry columns set and its rows restricted to term.

Examples

my_est <- label_estimator(
  function(data, ...) lm(Y ~ Z, data = data),
  label = "lm", inquiry = "ATE", term = "Z"
)
df <- data.frame(Y = rnorm(20), Z = rep(0:1, 10))
my_est(df)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   term  estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high estimator
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1 Z        0.291     0.576     0.505   0.619   -0.920      1.50 lm       
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: inquiry <chr>
